text: Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League match between Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest at the Vitality Stadium.
Struggling for form, two of the Premier League's bottom eight sides are in need of a morale-boosting victory here.
Bournemouth, who are 13th, are without a win in three, while 17th-place Forest are still seeking their first victory of 2024.
Andoni Iraola makes two changes from Bournemouth's 1-1 draw at West Ham in midweek.
Sinisterra and Kluivert come into the starting line-up with Scott and Tavernier dropping to the bench, where Ouattara returns following his participation at the Africa Cup of Nations.
The game is just too soon for new signing Eres Unal, who arrived on loan from Getafe, while the likes of Max Aarons, Tyler Adams and Ryan Fredericks are still absent due to injury.
As for Forest, Nuno Espirito Santo makes six alterations from the midweek defeat to Arsenal in an attempt to change his side's fortunes.
New signing Sels makes his debut in goal, while Gunners loanee Tavares returns after he was ineligible to face his parent club.

Yates, Hudson-Odoi, Elanga and Awoniyi are also back in the starting XI, while loan signings Reyna and Ribeiro could make their debuts from the bench, where Niakhate returns from the Africa Cup of Nations.
The Reds are without Divock Origi and Chris Wood due to injury, with Ola Aina, Willy Boly, Serge Aurier and Ibrahim Sangare away on international duty.
Forest have never won a Premier League match on a Sunday, losing five of their eight such matches.
They have also conceded at least three goals in each of those defeats.
Mind, Bournemouth have not fared much better.
The Cherries have lost 26 of their 37 Premier League matches on a Sunday, with their 70.3 per cent loss rate the highest among any side to have played at least 10 games on the day.
The teams are making their way out onto the field and we are almost ready to go here.
Rebecca Welch is our referee today.
She blows her whistle and Bournemouth get us under way.
Bournemouth threaten early on and Semenyo lays the ball off for Christie, whose drilled 20-yard effort deflects behind for a corner.

text: The Cherries are unbeaten in their last seven league meetings with Forest, winning five, stretching back to a 2-1 defeat in February 2015.
GOAL!!! 1-0 BOURNEMOUTH! What a start by the hosts! They take the lead after just five minutes.
Cook's inswinging corner is glanced on by Sinisterra.
Kluivert goes in at the far post to make sure, though it is unclear whether or not he touched the ball before it crossed the line.
Either way, the Cherries are in front.
Assist Luis Fernando Sinisterra Lucumí
It looks like it is Kluivert's goal.
Replays show the ball was on the goal-line when the midfielder applied the finishing touch.
That is now five goals in 13 games for him.
Bournemouth lead courtesy of only their 12th home goal of the season.
That is fewer than any other side in the Premier League.
Forest look to respond following a swift counter with Williams leading the charge.
He finds Gibbs-White, who in turn slips the ball through for Awoniyi.
However, the latter slips at the vital moment and his tame effort is easily gathered by Neto.
The Reds have now failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their last 12 Premier League matches.
Although, there is still a long way to go here and they have plenty of time to respond.
CHANCE! Forest steal possession in the centre circle and Dominguez finds Awoniyi, who skips past Senesi and advances into the area.
The angle is tight and his shot is a poor one that Neto gathers easily.
Bournemouth look to attack at the other end and Semenyo lines up a shot from distance.
His ambitious takes a deflection and is not too far wide of the far post.
Taking on Tavares, Semenyo forces Bournemouth's fifth corner of the match already.
Christie comes across to take it.
A worry for Bournemouth as Christie goes down not long after taking the corner.
He appeared to pick up a knock following a strong challenge from Dominguez a few moments ago, so it may be after-effects from that.
Senesi is very late with his sliding challenge on Hudson-Odoi.
The Bournemouth defender can have no complaints as he goes into the book.
CHANCE! Forest seek the equaliser and Gibbs-White sends a long free-kick into the box from the right flank.
Murillo helps the ball on and it drops kindly for Yates, whose shot is straight at Neto.
The Reds are in decent form on the road.
In fact, they have scored as many goals (six) and earned as many points (four) in their last three Premier League away games as they managed in their first eight this season.
We have hit the half-hour mark at the Vitality Stadium, where Bournemouth are still 1-0 to the good thanks to Kluivert's strike after just five minutes.
Kelly sends a long ball down the line looking for the run of Kluivert, but Omobamidele is quickly across to tidy up the situation.
Frustrated at not being awarded a free-kick after tangling with Yates, Kluivert then makes a silly challenge on Elanga and has his name taken.
Kluivert needs to be careful.
Having just received a yellow card, he then bundles Williams over.
The referee is not reaching for her pocket, but she will be keeping an eye on the Bournemouth midfielder.
Five minutes of the first half remain.
Nether side are carrying too much of an attacking threat as the clock ticks down towards the break.
Forest have lost eight of their last 11 Premier League games, the joint-most in the division since November 12.
They have also conceded the most goals in that time with 26.
HUDSON-ODOI!!! 1-1! FOREST ARE LEVEL! The visitors hit back just before the break.
After a free-kick is cleared, the ball breaks kindly for Hudson-Odoi, who skips inside before bending a 20-yard shot into the bottom-right corner.
Concern for Bournemouth as Semenyo stays down following that Forest equaliser.
He slipped awkwardly as the hosts looked to deal with the free-kick, and they will hope it is nothing too serious.
On his 200th Bournemouth appearance, Cook looks to help the hosts regain the lead by sending a free-kick into the box.
However, Sels comes a long way out of goal and makes a good punch to clear Forest lines.
Danger for Forest as a loose square ball by Tavares goes straight to Sinisterra.
The winger looks to capitalise, but his touch is too heavy and Sels comes out to collect.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
We are all square at the Vitality Stadium, where Bournemouth and Forest are deadlocked at 1-1.
The hosts took the lead in the fifth minute when Kluivert helped Sinisterra's header home from close range.
Although, the visitors levelled just before half-time when Hudson-Odoi curled a brilliant 20-yard effort into the bottom-right corner.
Forest enjoyed most of the possession during the first half (55.5 per cent) and all five of their shots were on target.
The visitors much continue in that vein if they are to potentially complete the turnaround here.
The hosts make a change at the break.
Semenyo, who was struggling towards the end of the first half, makes way for Tavernier.
We are off and running again at the Vitality Stadium.
Tavares sees headlines as he lines up an audacious shot from well over 30 yards out.
However, sarcastic cheers ring around the stadium as he fires the ball high into the stands.
Bournemouth are awarded a free-kick on the edge of the box after Yates challenges Tavernier from behind.
This is a promising position for the hosts.
Kluivert's free-kick goes straight into the wall and deflects behind for a corner.
However, Forest are able to deal with the set-piece and can relax for a moment.
Sinisterra tries to set Bournemouth moving as he looks for Solanke.
Although, Murillo is alert and able to dispossess the latter.
After Kluivert pushes him to the ground, Omobamidele is unhappy not to see a second yellow card shown to the Bournemouth midfielder.
His frustration sees the Forest defender receive one himself.
The hosts make a double-change.
The first of these sees Christie make way to be replaced by Scott.
Kluivert is also shrewdly withdrawn by Iraola.
Billing comes on in his place.
This contest is finely poised as we approach the final half an hour at the Vitality Stadium.
Who will grab the third goal of this game?
Bournemouth have won three of their last five Premier League home games, as many victories as they managed in their previous 16 such contests.
Following a Forest free-kick, a chance almost presents itself for Awoniyi.
However, the Bournemouth defence just about manage to scramble the ball away.
Awoniyi has been directly involved in 13 goals in his last 15 Premier League appearances, scoring 11 and assisting two.
Can he make a decisive impact today?
After dealing with a Bournemouth free-kick, Forest rapidly counter with Gibbs-White leading the charge.
However, they lose impetus as the hosts quickly recover numbers, before intercepting Dominguez's loose pass.
The Cherries threaten at the other end and Scott finds Sinisterra, who takes on his marker and looks to cross.
But his attempt to do so ricochets against him and behind for a goal kick.
That was one of Sinisterra's final actions of the game.
He goes off to be replaced by Ouattara.
The hardworking Dominguez is given a well-earned breather by Forest, with Danilo on in his place.
Yates catches Ouattara with a rash challenge and has his name taken by the referee.
An inswinging Bournemouth corner comes right into the six-yard box.
Although, under pressure from Scott, Sels does well to help the ball away from goal.
The hosts continue to threaten and are awarded a free-kick on the right flank.
Tavernier swings the ball in, but his delivery is disappointing and flashes behind for a goal kick.
Forest make two changes.
The first comes at right-back with Montiel replacing Williams.
There is a debut for loanee Reyna as he comes on in place of Elanga for the last 12 minutes.
There are 10 minutes remaining at the Vitality Stadium.
The match is there for the taking, but who will grab it by the scruff of the neck?
Ouattara, who has been lively since coming on, whips in a dangerous cross from the left wing.
With Solanke lurking, Murillo makes an important intervention by heading behind for a corner.
Bournemouth make a change at left-back with Kerkez introduced in favour of Kelly.
RED CARD FOR BILLING! Bournemouth are down to 10 men.
With Hudson-Odoi threatening to race away on the counter, Billing looks to stop him in his tracks and stamps down on the back of the Forest winger's Achilles.
Although the contact appeared to be accidental, it was dangerous and the referee shows him a straight red card.
Neto races out of goal to question the decision to send Billing off.
The Bournemouth skipper is booked for his troubles.
Billing's poor challenge left Hudson-Odoi in a lot of pain.
Thankfully, after limping towards the touchline, the Forst winger can eventually return to the action.
Unfortunately, Hudson-Odoi signals to the bench that he is unable to continue.
Helped from the field by a member of Forest's medical team, he is replaced by debutant Ribeiro.
SEVEN MINUTES! That is how long has been added on by the referee.
Can Forest capitalise on their numerical advantage?
We have reached the midway point in stoppage time at the end of this game.
Will we see a dramatic winner, or will the honours be shared?
Gibbs-White finds space and tries his luck from distance.
It is an ambitious attempt and a tame one that Neto easily collects.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
It finishes honours even at the Vitality Stadium, where Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest played out a 1-1 draw.
The hosts, who had an xG of 0.96 compared to 0.56 from their opponents, took the lead after just five minutes when Kluivert helped Sinisterra's header over the line.
The visitors equalised just before half-time thanks to Hudson-Odoi's curling 20-yard strike.
The Cherries finished with 10 men when substitute Billing was shown a straight red card six minutes from time, but the spoils were shared.
Both sides are back in Premier League action next Saturday with Bournemouth away at Fulham and Forest hosting Newcastle United.
Before that, the Reds welcome Bristol City to the City Ground on Wednesday for their FA Cup fourth-round replay.
Thanks for joining us today.
Until next time, goodbye!
